Rank-one normal inputs attain the largest eigenvalue. A 1,563-check deterministic independent Jacobian/difference-quotient script completed successfully; no finite sample is used as proof.

originality.rationale: The two-sided sampled projector and rank-one BUG update are old objects, and the motivating source gives a general finite-error relaxed-exactness estimate. Neither that statement nor the inspected two-sided projection optimality and BUG convergence theorems states the full Frechet singular spectrum or its sharp local coefficient. These are different quantifiers: the earlier coefficient sqrt(2+alpha^2+beta^2) bounds all increment defects, whereas this result determines the true infinitesimal operator norm sqrt(1+alpha^2+beta^2). The exact derivative can be derived from existing formulas, so unindexed prior equivalent derivations remain a specific priority risk.

value.rationale: The complete dimension-independent derivative singular spectrum is a structural error-channel classification of a numerically important same-increment BUG update: the tangent block is copied, normal residuals enter two different tangent components, and some tangent-normal combinations cancel to first order. Sharp singular values yield a basis-angle tolerance for local increment errors and a matching worst-case perturbation. This directly clarifies the gap between unconditional finite-error robustness estimates and small-defect sensitivity; it is more informative than a trivial special-case restatement of a bound, while not claiming a new algorithm or global improvement.
